clue.text: Diving in, it helps to take a deep breath

definitions.text: Diving in, it helps to take a deep breath

parts.words: Diving in, it helps to take a deep breath
parts.note: reads like advice to fill your lungs before a plunge, but describes the breathing apparatus a diver carries underwater

explanation.walkthrough: The clue sounds like a tip for swimmers holding their breath; in fact the device supplies the deep breaths while you are down there.
explanation.definitionFit: A diver's breathing equipment lets the wearer breathe deeply while submerged, so the cryptic description fits it exactly.

clue.text: Very keen on prima donna's come-uppance

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is brought up, so its letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a prima donna is an opera diva

explanation.surface: Someone takes delight in seeing a haughty opera star humbled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'come-uppance' looks like a deserved punishment, but split as come-up it tells you to send DIVA upwards in this down light, giving AVID.
explanation.definitionFit: Avid is a straightforward synonym for very keen or eager, as in an avid reader.

clue.text: Glibness is no such thing!

parts.note: the letters of the word glibness are a jumbled version of a word for a boon, so glibness is that boon mixed up, and not the pure form

explanation.walkthrough: GLIBNESS is an anagram of BLESSING, so it is literally a mixed blessing; therefore it is not an unmixed one.
explanation.definitionFit: A pure benefit with no drawback is a total boon; glibness, being scrambled, is the opposite.

clue.text: Influence announcement of prize, given time —

parts.note: prize said out loud is prise, the tool for forcing a lid open, which is a lever
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Someone wields power over the declaration of an award, with a deadline attached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'announcement of prize' is prize as heard: prise, a bar used to force things open, which is a LEVER; add AGE. The dash runs the clue on into 4 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Leverage is power to sway a situation or person, a common synonym for influence.

clue.text: - a prize being presented by peer turning up at last

indicators.note: in this down clue the final pair of letters is turned upwards, so only that end stretch is read in reverse

parts.note: a peer is a noble, a member of the aristocracy

explanation.surface: An award is handed out by a lord who arrives late, carrying on from 3 down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up at last' turns only the last two letters of NOBLE, so LE becomes EL, giving NOBEL.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nobel is the famous international award founded by Alfred Nobel, so it is an example of a prize.

clue.text: Building up, quickly, description of Beatles' early days?

definitions.meaning: a building put up fast from factory-made sections
the Beatles were the Fab Four, so their early days came before the Fab

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a playful split: PRE plus FAB, the time before the Fab Four became famous.
explanation.definitionFit: A prefab is a house built rapidly from ready-made parts, and pre-Fab jokily names the Beatles' early period.

clue.text: Tease a Lord, being risqué

parts.note: to rib someone is to tease them

explanation.surface: Making fun of a peer turns out to be rather daring.
explanation.definitionFit: Ribald humour is coarse and suggestive, which is what risqué means.

clue.text: Its members are instructed to come out

definitions.text: Its members are instructed to come out

parts.words: Its members are instructed to come out
parts.note: sounds like a strike call to union members, but describes young ladies being trained for their debut in society

explanation.walkthrough: 'come out' is not a walkout: a debutante comes out into society, and these establishments polished girls for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A school teaching young women social graces prepared them to make their debut, or come out, in society.

clue.text: Promise to support part of Norfolk, given means of attack

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits beneath the other one

parts.note: the Norfolk Broads are a network of rivers and lakes in the English county of Norfolk
to give your word is to promise

explanation.surface: Someone pledges to back a region of Norfolk, armed with a way of fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to support' puts WORD below BROADS in this down answer. The Broads are a famous waterway area in Norfolk, eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadsword is a heavy wide-bladed sword, an instrument used for attacking.

clue.text: Spread of notes out of sequence finished

indicators.note: the musical letters are rearranged rather than kept in alphabetical order

parts.note: B, C, D and E are among the musical notes A to G
over means finished or ended

explanation.surface: A musical score spread out of order has come to an end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of sequence' rearranges the notes B C D E into BEDC; add OVER.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedspread is a cover laid over a bed, so spread here means that coverlet.

clue.text: I can set about second verse fast

indicators.note: the first words are placed around the next pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: I can is equivalent to I'm able
MO, short for moment, is a second

explanation.surface: Someone says they can tackle the second stanza without budging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' looks like speedy but means firmly fixed. 'set about' wraps the expansion of 'I can' around MO and V; MO is British shorthand for a moment, as in 'half a mo'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fast in the sense of firmly fixed, as in stuck fast, means unable to be moved.

clue.text: Stop "the little woman" being something that's played on

parts.note: to ban something is to stop it
Jo March is one of the sisters in the novel Little Women

explanation.surface: A request to silence a man's wife, who is otherwise a source of amusement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the little woman' sounds like an old-fashioned term for a wife, but points to Jo, one of the Little Women.
explanation.definitionFit: A banjo is a stringed instrument, so it is something a musician plays on.

clue.text: Dog initially failing to make a jump?

indicators.note: the first letter goes missing, failing to appear at the start

parts.note: a boxer is a breed of dog

explanation.surface: A dog fails at its first attempt at a leap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially failing' means BOXER loses its first letter, B, giving OXER.
explanation.definitionFit: In show jumping an oxer is a fence made of two sets of rails, a type of obstacle horses leap.

clue.text: Pub side thrashed in specific area

parts.note: a local is a person's neighbourhood pub

indicators.note: a beaten-up word is knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: The team from the pub was beaten in their own particular patch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrashed' suggests a beaten team, but it scrambles the side into ISED. A local is the British term for the pub nearest your home that you regularly visit.
explanation.definitionFit: Localised means confined to a particular place, which is restricted to one specific area.

clue.text: On a trip in Wales with aging Celt?

indicators.note: being on a trip suggests letters wandering off and coming back rearranged

explanation.surface: An elderly Celt is travelling through Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On a trip' rearranges WALES and AGING. A native of Glasgow is a Scot, and so a Celt, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Glasgow is Scottish and Scots are Celtic, so this is a definition by example.

clue.text: She barely tolerated being sent to Coventry

definitions.text: She barely tolerated being sent to Coventry

parts.words: She barely tolerated being sent to Coventry
parts.note: sounds like someone grudgingly enduring being ostracised, but describes the legendary noblewoman who rode naked through Coventry

explanation.walkthrough: 'sent to Coventry' is a British idiom for being shunned, and 'barely' means without clothes: the legend has her ride naked through Coventry's streets.
explanation.definitionFit: The eleventh-century noblewoman of legend rode unclothed through Coventry, so the clue paints her literally.

clue.text: James perhaps put record on new pile

indicators.note: in a down answer the piece placed on top comes first

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record

indicators.note: something made new is rearranged, here the letters of pile

explanation.surface: A man named James puts a record on top of a fresh heap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns PILE into IPLE, placed under DISC. James was one of Jesus's twelve apostles.
explanation.definitionFit: James was one of the twelve followers of Jesus, so he is an example of a disciple.

clue.text: Opinion to contend with

parts.note: to vie is to contend or compete

explanation.surface: A point of view that must be dealt with.
explanation.definitionFit: A view is a personal opinion, as in in my view.

clue.text: Musician with outrageous suit in apartment

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are placed inside the word for an apartment

parts.note: a flat is an apartment

indicators.note: something outrageous is wild, so the letters run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: A player in a garish outfit sits in their flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outrageous' reads as describing a loud outfit, but it jumbles the suit into UTIS; 'in' then sets that inside the British word for an apartment.
explanation.definitionFit: A flautist plays the flute, so is a kind of musician.

clue.text: Take this when you go into a particular kind of bar

definitions.text: Take this when you go into a particular kind of bar

parts.words: Take this when you go into a particular kind of bar
parts.note: suggests ordering a drink in a pub, but refers to a barrister being promoted to senior rank at the legal bar

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a barrister made Queen's (now King's) Counsel is said to take silk, from the silk gown worn; the bar is the legal profession, not a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Becoming a senior barrister is called taking silk, so silk is what one takes at that bar.

clue.text: I may warn of future problems, having surveyed houses

definitions.text: I may warn of future problems, having surveyed houses

parts.words: I may warn of future problems, having surveyed houses
parts.note: sounds like a building surveyor's report, but the houses are the twelve divisions of the zodiac chart studied by a fortune-teller

explanation.walkthrough: 'houses' are the twelve sectors of a horoscope, not buildings.
explanation.definitionFit: A stargazer who reads the zodiac's houses claims to foresee trouble, matching this description.

clue.text: Pull off smash-and-grab raid somewhere in the country

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held and printed as 'Pull off smash-and-grab raid somewhere in the country (6)' for INVADE: no parse found; 'raid' could define it but no wordplay builds INVADE from the rest, and a search of the exact text finds nothing.
annotationWithheld.clue: Pull off smash-and-grab raid somewhere in the country

clue.text: So is certain oil-production absolutely necessary?

definitions.meaning: an oil distilled from a plant, like lavender oil, is described with this word
indispensable, something you cannot do without

explanation.walkthrough: Essential oil is the term for an aromatic plant extract, giving the first sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means indispensable, and also names the class of fragrant oils pressed from plants.

clue.text: Cruel machination for ill-gotten gain

indicators.note: a machination is scheming manipulation, so the letters are manipulated into another order

explanation.surface: A cruel plot to get rich dishonestly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'machination for' rearranges CRUEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucre, as in filthy lucre, is money, especially money gained dishonourably.

clue.text: Contents of The Sun could appear strange to 14

indicators.note: the letters inside the run of words are picked out, the way a container holds contents

explanation.surface: Something in a tabloid newspaper might seem odd to a Glasgow reader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contents of' points inside 'Sun could'. Unco is a Scots word for strange, so it is how a Glaswegian (14 down) would say it.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots dialect unco means strange or unusual, so it is the word a Glasgow speaker uses.

clue.text: Arab possibly staked £25

definitions.meaning: an Arab is a breed of horse, so a small horse may be one
in British betting slang twenty-five pounds has a horsey nickname, a sum one might stake on a bet

explanation.walkthrough: British slang names sums of money: £25 is this small horse, £500 a monkey.
explanation.definitionFit: An Arab is a horse breed, and British betting slang calls a sum of twenty-five pounds by this name.

clue.text: Business done briefly after one contacts a holiday resort

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
biz is a short informal form of the word business

explanation.surface: A firm's work is wrapped up quickly before somebody gets in touch about a getaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after one' places BIZ after I, and 'contacts' means it touches A.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibiza is a Spanish Balearic island famous as a holiday destination.

clue.text: Offence almost taken during a solo turn, sadly for musician

indicators.note: the shortened word is placed inside the other letters
a turn here means a change of order, so the letters are rearranged
the last letter is dropped, leaving nearly the whole word

parts.note: a crime is an offence against the law

explanation.surface: An offender is nearly caught during a solo performance, which saddens the player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' is the anagram signal, not a performance slot: it makes LAOSO. 'almost' trims the offence, and 'taken during' sets it inside. The definition is an Italian score direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacrimoso is an Italian performance direction telling a musician to play mournfully, that is, sadly.

clue.text: Maxim perhaps recalled to acquire a bit of gold

indicators.note: called back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: the Maxim was an early machine gun
to get is to acquire

explanation.surface: A saying is remembered so that one can pick up a small piece of wisdom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maxim' looks like a saying, but it is the Maxim machine gun; 'recalled' turns GUN into NUG.
explanation.definitionFit: A nugget is a small lump of gold found in nature.

clue.text: Fellows agree how intelligence is developed

parts.note: men are fellows
to tally is to agree or match up

explanation.surface: A group of chaps concur on how the mind grows.
explanation.definitionFit: Intelligence is something exercised in the mind, so it develops in a mind-based way, which this adverb expresses.
